definition: In historical witchcraft belief, imps were imagined as small evil helper spirits that carried out a witch’s commands. They appear in accounts as attendants associated with witches and the devil.

reasons: “Small” is not supported by the packet; the source only says witches’ behests were carried out by “imps and familiars.”
“Evil helper spirits” overstates the source, which does not define imps as a class of spirits or explicitly as helpers; it only mentions them in witchcraft accounts.
“Attendants associated with witches and the devil” is only loosely implied, not stated as a definition, so the wording goes beyond the packet’s support.
The packet supports that witches’ “behests were carried out by imps and familiars,” but it does not describe imps as “small,” “evil,” or as “helper spirits.”

The packet does connect imps with the witch/devil context (e.g., testimony of accused dancing “with imps” or “with the devil”), but the definition’s specific phrasing “attendants associated with witches and the devil” is not fully supported as such.
Because multiple substantive descriptors (“small,” “evil helper spirits,” “attendants”) are not explicitly present in the provided packet, the definition overreaches beyond the supplied source.
